links.outcome: Shift in ESI triage output when only one demographic or socioeconomic variable is changed
links.effect: Counterfactual sensitivity varied substantially and did not consistently decrease with model size or medical pretraining; fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B had 5.27% any-shift rate vs 16.02% for base model.
links.quote: Counterfactual sensitivity varied substantially and did not consistently decrease with larger model size or medical-domain pretraining.

links.outcome: Hidden directional and shared failure patterns masked by aggregate rates in triage predictions
links.effect: Stratified and correlation analyses revealed clinically important directionality and shared failure patterns hidden by aggregate rates; several larger or medical-domain models showed more significant shifts.
links.quote: Stratified and correlation analyses further revealed clinically important directionality and shared failure patterns hidden by aggregate rates.

unlisted_practices: Using lightweight counterfactual auditing to compare open-source LLM fairness risks before clinical deployment
Fine-tuning (QLoRA) an open-source model to reduce counterfactual sensitivity in triage

screen.reason: The study empirically develops and evaluates a counterfactual auditing framework to evaluate bias and fairness across multiple open-source LLMs before clinical deployment.

primary.practice: counterfactual fairness auditing / pre-deployment bias testing
